QF.id: AIF Valuation Taxation and Good Practices_23

question.text: Business vs investment income matters because:

answer.text: Business income is taxed at fund level even for Cat I/II (not pass-through)
Investment income is always taxed higher

explanation.text: The Logic: For Category I and II Investment Funds, income other than business income is pass-through and is taxed in the hands of investors. Business income, by contrast, is taxable at the Investment Fund level and is exempt in the investors' hands, which is why the character of the income matters for the tax outcome. The Finance Act 2025 clarification that securities held by Category I/II AIFs are capital assets further supports the investment-income characterisation. The Trap: Claiming business income is always tax-free, that there is no distinction, or that investment income is always taxed higher each contradicts the workbook's specific split between pass-through investment income and fund-level business income. Note: Based on NISM Series XIX-A workbook pages 253, 254, 258, and 259, which describe the business-vs-investment-income split and the Finance Act 2025 capital-asset clarification.
